questions.q: Where is a Required checkbox enforced?
options: Only in the Salesforce UI, not through the API or imports
Everywhere a record can be created or edited — UI, API, import, and automation
Only during a data import
Only when Advanced Currency Management is enabled
questions.explain: Required blocks a blank save universally — through the UI, the API, imports, and automation like Flow.

questions.q: What does marking a field Unique actually do?
options: It rejects a save if the value already exists on another record of the same object
It makes the field read-only
It automatically generates a new value for every record
It hides the field from reports
questions.explain: Unique enforces that no two records of the object can share the same value in that field, with an option for case-sensitive or case-insensitive matching.

questions.q: What does checking External ID make a field usable for?
options: Nothing beyond cosmetic labeling
The matching key in an upsert, letting an integration update existing records or insert new ones based on that value
Automatically deleting duplicate records
Converting the field into a Formula field
questions.explain: External ID indexes the field and allows it to serve as the match key for an upsert operation against an outside system.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, Upsert(sObjectType, "Legacy_Customer_Id__c", records) — what role does Legacy_Customer_Id__c play?
options: It's the object being upserted
It's the External ID field Salesforce uses to decide whether to update an existing record or insert a new one
It's a Roll-Up Summary field
It's unrelated to the upsert operation
questions.explain: The second argument to an upsert call is the External ID field used as the matching key between incoming records and existing Salesforce records.

questions.q: Which two properties does this lesson say commonly work together on the same field?
options: Required and Picklist
Unique and External ID
Formula and Roll-Up Summary
Master-Detail and Checkbox
questions.explain: A field is very often marked both Unique (no duplicate key collides) and External ID (the field an integration matches on) at the same time.
